title: Plan your game: your topic, who it is for, and your 4 games
kind: a planning chapter, before you open Visual Studio 2019
one: You choose the topic of your game and who will play it, and you give your game a name. Then you pick the 4 games you will build, and say what each one becomes in your game.

stages.title: Choose your topic, who your game is for, and its name

screens.title: Choose a topic and the people who will play your game

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know the topic of your game, who it is for, and what it is called.

words: What your game teaches or practises, such as French verbs, the parts of a cell or the steps of a dance.
The people who will play your game, such as primary school pupils, KS3 pupils or the members of a club.
blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

blocks.p: Your [[topic|0]] is what your game teaches or practises. Pick something that people find tricky, or want to get better at.
It can be a school subject and a topic in it, such as the parts of a plant cell in KS3 Science.
It can also be something outside school, such as the steps taught at a local dance class, or the rules of a sport.
Your [[audience|1]] is the people who will play your game. For example, primary school pupils, KS3, GCSE or A-level pupils, or the members of a club.
Your audience changes how you write your game. Words for primary school pupils are shorter and simpler than words for A-level pupils.

box.title: An example to read: the topic and audience of Summit Ready

blocks.p: **Topic:** the skills for a first hill-walking expedition, such as what to pack, grid references and timing a route.
**Audience:** pupils aged 14 to 16 going on their first expedition.
**Name:** Summit Ready.
Give your game a short name with no spaces. In chapter 2, it becomes the name of your Visual Studio 2019 project, the folder that holds your game's files.
For example, a game called Dance Steps is a project called `DanceSteps`.

screens.title: Pick 4 of the 8 games, and say what each one becomes

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know which 4 games you will build, and what each one is about in your game.
Chapters 11 to 18 each build one game. You build any 4 of them. You may build more than 4 if you have time.
Pick the games that suit your topic best. Here is what each game is, without the hill-walking.
**Chapter 11, Pack the Rucksack:** a sorting game. The player drags each thing into the right group.
**Chapter 12, Knot Pairs:** a memory game. The player turns over cards to find the pairs.
**Chapter 13, Leave No Trace:** an arcade game. The player moves with the keyboard, picks up the right things and keeps away from the others.
**Chapter 14, Read the Sky:** a picture quiz against the clock.
**Chapter 15, Whiteout:** a hidden-word game. The player guesses the word one letter at a time, from a clue.
**Chapter 16, Grid Ref Rescue:** a grid game. A picture is cut into a 10 by 10 grid, and the player finds a square.
**Chapter 17, Route Timer:** an estimating game. The player moves a slider to estimate a number, such as how long a walk takes.
**Chapter 18, Listen Out:** a listening game. A sound plays, and the player picks what made it.

box.title: An example to read: 4 games for a game about a local dance class

blocks.p: **Pack the Rucksack** becomes sorting each move into the dance it belongs to.
**Knot Pairs** becomes matching each step to its name.
**Route Timer** becomes estimating how many counts a move takes.
**Listen Out** becomes playing a piece of music, and picking the dance it is for.
You can change your mind about a game at any time before chapter 11.
You also choose how many points each question in your game is worth. The game chapters show you where to set them.
Run each check below before you go on to chapter 2. Tick each check when it is true for you.

check.how: If your game is about mountains, camping, knots or the weather, it is too close to Summit Ready. Pick another topic.

check.what: Your game has a name, and you know its project name with no spaces.
